result.title: TIDE: Tree-Induced Fine-Grained Diagnostic Evaluation from Model Behaviors
result.summary: Benchmark performance is the dominant standard for comparing large language models (LLMs), typically summarized by a single aggregate score, such as accuracy, pass rate, or rubric score. This aggregate score provides limited information about a model's underlying capabilities, yet understanding these capabilities is crucial for model development and evaluation. To this end, we propose Tree-Induced Diagnostic Evaluation (TIDE), which recasts diagnostic evaluation as behavior-driven decision-tree induction to perform fine-grained capability diagnosis. TIDE recursively builds a hierarchical capability tree from benchmark samples and model scores: at each node, an LLM judge proposes candidate splits and performs sample-to-group classification, and behavior-based information gain selects among them. We apply TIDE to five models across four benchmarks to demonstrate its effectiveness, and find fine-grained capability contrasts invisible at the aggregate level: Claude Opus 4.6 achieves 100% on microeconomic market reasoning where GPT-5.4 scores 83.3%, but trails GPT-5.4 on contract law reasoning with 77.8% versus 88.9%. We hope TIDE can be extended to past and future benchmarks so that the rich behavioral signal in evaluation results is fully leveraged for understanding model capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TIDE，把诊断式评测表述为行为驱动的决策树归纳：由 LLM judge 在基准样本上提出候选划分并按信息增益选择，递归构建层级能力树，从而在四个基准、五个模型上揭示聚合分数掩盖的细粒度能力差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其行为驱动、按样本属性递归划分的诊断思路，可能用于细粒度归因 VLM 推理成败中视觉证据与任务属性的贡献，为「答案是否使用 latent 内容」提供评价工具线索；但材料仅涉及纯文本基准，迁移可行性需核查。
